reforms.description: The federal government set aside funds for financing pilot projects in carbon capture and storage (CCS) to address greenhouse gas emissions from oil sands production, supporting technological breakthroughs in emissions reduction.
reforms.package_name: Climate Change and Environmental Policy Framework
reforms.component_name: Carbon Capture and Storage Pilot Projects
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Supports development of emissions-reducing technologies that enable continued resource extraction while addressing climate constraints, enhancing long-term productivity and competitiveness in the energy sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'the federal government has set aside funds for financing pilot projects in carbon capture and storage,' indicating an announced commitment.
reforms.importance_rationale: A targeted sectoral R&D initiative addressing a significant environmental and economic challenge (oil sands emissions), with potential for meaningful technological impact, but narrower in scope than system-wide innovation reforms.
reforms.source_quote: In that context, the federal government has set aside funds for financing pilot projects in carbon capture and storage.

reforms.description: The federal government provided substantial budgetary support for research and development into cellulose-based ethanol production to improve efficiency, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and boost farmer incomes as part of the nation-wide bio-energy effort.
reforms.package_name: Climate Change and Environmental Policy Framework
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D support for renewable energy technology can enhance long-term productivity and competitiveness, but the text questions the emissions-saving benefits and cost efficiency, suggesting uncertain net growth effects.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'substantial budgetary support for research and development has been granted,' indicating the programme is in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: A sectoral R&D programme with significant budgetary commitment to agricultural biofuels, but the Survey questions its premises and cost-effectiveness, suggesting limited long-term importance.
reforms.source_quote: The hope has been that producing ethanol from cellulose would promise better returns, and substantial budgetary support for research and development has been granted.

reforms.description: Canada provides R&D tax credits to firms, with a higher rate (35%) for small firms compared to large firms (20%). This is a significant federal corporate tax expenditure designed to incentivize private-sector research and development.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax credits reduce the cost of innovation for firms, incentivizing private investment in research and development, which generates positive spillovers and enhances long-run productivity and competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'small firms can claim federal R&D credits at a rate of 35% against only 20% for large firms' and lists 'SR&ED tax credit' as the fifth largest tax expenditure in 2007, indicating the programme is in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: The R&D tax credit is a significant and long-standing innovation instrument with substantial budgetary impact (CAD 4.3 billion in 2007, growing 122% from 2002–2009). It is a core mechanism for incentivizing private-sector R&D, though the text raises questions about the efficiency of the small-firm preference.
reforms.source_quote: Furthermore, small firms can claim federal R&D credits at a rate of 35% against only 20% for large firms.

reforms.description: Canada's SR&ED (Scientific Research and Experimental Development) tax credit provides substantial federal and provincial tax assistance for private R&D spending, with an effective marginal subsidy of approximately 120% for large firms. The credit applies to eligible current spending, primarily wages, and is complemented by provincial add-ons.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax credits address knowledge spillover externalities and encourage private investment in innovation, though empirical evidence on productivity payoff remains mixed. The scheme aims to stimulate firm-level R&D investment and technological development.
reforms.status_evidence: The text describes the SR&ED credit as currently operating: 'Canada offers one of the most generous rates of R&D tax assistance among a large group of OECD and emerging market countries' and notes that '32% of the total value of SR&ED tax credits goes to small firms'.
reforms.importance_rationale: The SR&ED credit is among the top 10 federal tax expenditures in Canada and represents a significant ongoing instrument for stimulating private R&D. However, the text notes that multifactor productivity statistics have not yet shown substantial payoff, and the scheme's effectiveness is questioned, suggesting it is a major but potentially inefficient instrument.
reforms.source_quote: Canada offers one of the most generous rates of R&D tax assistance among a large group of OECD and emerging market countries. The effective marginal subsidy (reduction in the METR) for large firms is close to 120% (as compared with 30% in the United States).

reforms.description: The text discusses the need to evaluate Canada's R&D credit scheme for 'value for money' and proposes potential reform to unify tax credit rates for small, Canadian-owned, and large firms at a lower level (20% rather than 35%) to improve public returns on R&D investment.
reforms.component_name: Unification of small and large firm credit rates
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Unifying credit rates at a lower level could improve allocative efficiency by directing R&D subsidies toward firms with greater capacity to generate returns, potentially increasing the overall productivity impact of public R&D support.
reforms.status_evidence: The text presents this as a policy recommendation: 'Future research should look into whether unifying the tax credits for small, Canadian-owned and large firms – respectively 35 and 20% – at the lower level would raise the public's rate of return'.
reforms.importance_rationale: This proposed reform would restructure a major tax expenditure instrument to improve efficiency and targeting. It represents a significant but narrower reform focused on optimizing an existing scheme rather than creating new capacity.
reforms.source_quote: Future research should look into whether unifying the tax credits for small, Canadian-owned and large firms – respectively 35 and 20% – at the lower level would raise the public's rate of return insofar as large and foreign firms may be better placed to undertake R&D investments.

reforms.description: Canada raised the ceiling for access to SR&ED (Scientific Research and Experimental Development) enhanced investment tax credits from CAD 15 million to CAD 50 million in taxable capital, broadening eligibility for small firms to claim R&D tax incentives.
reforms.component_name: SR&ED Enhanced Investment Tax Credit Expansion
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Expands R&D incentives for small firms, lowering the cost of innovation investment and encouraging private-sector R&D activity that raises productivity and competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states: 'In the 2008 budget, the definition of what constitutes a "small" firm was eased in the case of access to the SR&ED enhanced investment tax credits: the ceiling was raised from CAD 15 million of taxable capital to CAD 50 million.'
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant but targeted expansion of an existing R&D tax instrument that broadens access for small firms. The measure increases the pool of eligible firms and reduces barriers to claiming R&D credits, supporting private-sector innovation capacity.
reforms.source_quote: In the 2008 budget, the definition of what constitutes a "small" firm was eased in the case of access to the SR&ED enhanced investment tax credits: the ceiling was raised from CAD 15 million of taxable capital to CAD 50 million.

reforms.description: An evaluation of the Federal Tax Credit for Scientific Research and Experimental Development was conducted, assessing the effectiveness and design of this R&D tax incentive instrument.
reforms.package_name: Federal Tax Credit for Scientific Research and Experimental Development
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The text reports only that an evaluation was conducted; the actual findings and their implications for growth are not disclosed in this excerpt.
reforms.status_evidence: A Department of Finance Working Paper evaluating the tax credit was published in September 2007.
reforms.importance_rationale: This is an evaluation study of an existing instrument rather than a new policy reform. It represents an analytical exercise to assess the effectiveness of an established R&D tax credit, which is incremental in nature.
reforms.source_quote: Parsons, M. and N. Phillips (2007), 'An Evaluation of the Federal Tax Credit for Scientific Research and Experimental Development', Department of Finance Working Paper, 2007-08, Ottawa, September.

reforms.description: Canada announced a new Science and Technology strategy titled 'Mobilising Science and Technology to Canada's Advantage' in May 2007, based on four core principles: promoting world-class excellence, focusing on priorities, encouraging partnerships, and enhancing accountability.
reforms.package_name: Mobilising Science and Technology to Canada's Advantage
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: A clearly articulated national S&T strategy with focus on excellence and priorities should improve the allocation and effectiveness of public R&D spending, supporting productivity and innovation-driven growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Canada announced a new S&T strategy in May 2007 based on four core principles.
reforms.importance_rationale: This is a system-wide strategic framework for national science and technology policy, establishing integrated priorities and governance principles across the entire public research system. It represents a major structural reform in how Canada articulates and implements its innovation policy.
reforms.source_quote: In May 2007 Canada announced a new S&T strategy, Mobilising Science and Technology to Canada's Advantage, which is based on four core principles: promoting world-class excellence, focussing on priorities, encouraging partnerships, and enhancing accountability.

reforms.description: Canada modified the SR&ED (Scientific Research and Experimental Development) tax credit scheme by adjusting phase-out limits for small businesses in the 2008 budget to reduce disincentives to growth.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Reducing disincentives to growth in the SR&ED tax credit encourages small businesses to expand their R&D activities and scale up, supporting innovation and productivity growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Changes to the phase-out limits for access to the enhanced SR&ED benefits for small businesses in the 2008 budget will reduce the disincentive to growth.
reforms.importance_rationale: A targeted refinement of an existing major R&D tax credit instrument to improve its effectiveness for small businesses. Significant but narrower in scope than a system-wide reform, addressing a specific design flaw that discouraged firm growth.
reforms.source_quote: Changes to the phase-out limits for access to the enhanced SR&ED benefits for small businesses in the 2008 budget will reduce the disincentive to growth.

reforms.description: Canada emphasized better collaboration between public research institutions and the private sector to improve commercialization outcomes and provide targeted innovation assistance for businesses as part of its strategy 'Mobilising Science and Technology to Canada's Advantage'.
reforms.package_name: Mobilising Science and Technology to Canada's Advantage
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthening linkages between public research and the private sector improves the translation of research into commercial innovation, enhancing productivity and competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: Canada is emphasising better collaboration between public research institutions and the private sector to improve commercialisation outcomes and provide targeted innovation assistance for businesses as part of its strategy, Mobilising Science and Technology to Canada's Advantage, released in May 2007.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant policy emphasis on strengthening university-industry linkages and commercialization as part of the broader S&T strategy. Meaningful but narrower than a structural system reform, focusing on improving knowledge transfer mechanisms.
reforms.source_quote: Canada is emphasising better collaboration between public research institutions and the private sector to improve commercialisation outcomes and provide targeted innovation assistance for businesses as part of its strategy, Mobilising Science and Technology to Canada's Advantage, released in May 2007.

reforms.description: The federal government announced a Science and Technology Strategy focusing public R&D funding on priority areas including environmental science and technologies, and natural resources and energy, integrating energy and environmental concerns into the national innovation system.
reforms.component_name: Priority area funding for environmental and energy R&D
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Directs public R&D toward sectors with high social and economic value, addressing market failures in environmental innovation and building technological capabilities in strategic sectors.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'In its Science and Technology Strategy, the federal government indicated its willingness to focus funding on priority areas' and references Government of Canada 2007b.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant strategic reorientation of federal R&D funding toward priority sectors (environmental science, energy, natural resources), but implementation and actual budget allocation remain uncertain at the time of writing.
reforms.source_quote: In its Science and Technology Strategy, the federal government indicated its willingness to focus funding on priority areas that are in the national interest from a social and economic perspective. This includes environmental science and technologies, and natural resources and energy.

reforms.description: The federal government allocated CAD 240 million in the 2008 budget to Saskatchewan for a full-scale commercial demonstration of carbon capture and storage (CCS) technology in the coal-fired electricity sector, to be matched by the province and partnered with industry.
reforms.component_name: Carbon capture and storage demonstration project
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Supports development of a technology with significant export potential and comparative advantage for Canada, addressing climate mitigation while building technological capabilities in a strategic sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'The 2008 federal Budget provides CAD 240 million in trust in the fiscal year 2007 to Saskatchewan' for this initiative.
reforms.importance_rationale: A substantial sectoral R&D investment in a specific technology with strategic importance, but narrower in scope than a system-wide reform; demonstrates commitment to applied energy research and public-private collaboration.
reforms.source_quote: The 2008 federal Budget provides CAD 240 million in trust in the fiscal year 2007 to Saskatchewan for this initiative, which will be matched by the province and used to partner with industry.

reforms.description: A CAD 550 million fund was established in 2002 for Sustainable Development Technology Canada to address the funding gap at the demonstration and pre-commercialisation stages, supporting environmental innovation projects prior to venture capital investment.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Addresses market failure in financing the demonstration and pre-commercialisation stages of environmental technologies, reducing capital constraints for innovative firms and accelerating technology deployment.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'A fund of CAD 550 million provided to Sustainable Development Technology Canada was established in 2002' and notes it 'has been successful in providing support to 133 projects'.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant and established innovation financing instrument with demonstrated track record (133 projects, over CAD 1 billion in total investment), though the text notes limitations in scope (Canadian firms only, concentration on SMEs).
reforms.source_quote: A fund of CAD 550 million provided to Sustainable Development Technology Canada was established in 2002 to address the gap in funding at the demonstration and pre-commercialisation stages, just prior to venture capital investment. The Fund has been successful in providing support to 133 projects involving over a billion dollars of investment thus far.

reforms.description: The federal government created the EcoENERGY Technology Initiative with CAD 230 million to reduce air pollutants and greenhouse gas emissions from conventional energy sources and increase Canada's supply of clean energy, including through development of alternative, sustainable energy technologies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Directs public R&D funding toward clean energy technology development, which can enhance long-term productivity and competitiveness in the energy sector while addressing environmental constraints.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states the initiative was created and allocated CAD 230 million, indicating active implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant sectoral R&D initiative with substantial funding (CAD 230 million) targeting clean energy technology development, representing a meaningful but focused intervention in energy innovation.
reforms.source_quote: creating the EcoENERGY Technology Initiative (CAD230million) to reduce air pollutants and GHG emissions from conventional energy sources and increase Canada's supply of clean energy, including through the development of alternative, sustainable energy technologies

reforms.description: The 2007 federal Budget allocated CAD 15 million to advance collaborative academic research in energy recovery and alternative energy development, and created the Canada EcoTrust for Clean Air and Climate Change to support relevant provincial and territorial projects.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Funds collaborative research and knowledge transfer between academic institutions and provincial/territorial partners to develop clean energy technologies, supporting innovation capacity and regional development.
reforms.status_evidence: The 2007 Budget allocated funds and created the EcoTrust, indicating active implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: A meaningful sectoral R&D initiative combining direct research funding (CAD 15 million) with a trust mechanism for collaborative projects, supporting applied research in clean energy across multiple jurisdictions.
reforms.source_quote: The2007Budget provided CAD15million to advance collaborative academic research in these areas and create the Canada EcoTrust for Clean Air and Climate Change to support relevant provincial and territorial projects.

reforms.description: The federal government announced the ecoENERGY for Biofuels Initiative on 5 July 2007, investing up to CAD 1.5 billion over nine years to boost Canada's production of biofuels such as ethanol and biodiesel.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Directs substantial public R&D investment toward biofuels development, supporting technological advancement in renewable energy production and creating new industrial capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states the federal government 'announced the creation' of the initiative on 5 July 2007.
reforms.importance_rationale: A major sectoral R&D initiative with substantial funding (CAD 1.5 billion over nine years) targeting a strategic energy technology area, representing a significant structural commitment to biofuels development and clean energy transition.
reforms.source_quote: On 5July2007, the federal government announced the creation of the ecoENERGY for Biofuels Initiative, which will invest up to CAD1.5billion over nine years to boost Canada's production of biofuels such as ethanol and biodiesel.

reforms.description: The 2007 federal Budget allocated CAD 500 million for large facilities producing 'next generation' renewables, with the government committed to facilitating the commercialisation of cellulose ethanol.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Funds development of large-scale facilities for next-generation renewable fuel production, supporting both research infrastructure and commercialisation of advanced biofuel technologies.
reforms.status_evidence: The 2007 Budget allocated CAD 500 million for these facilities, indicating policy announcement.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant component of biofuels policy with substantial capital allocation (CAD 500 million) for research infrastructure and commercialisation of advanced renewable technologies.
reforms.source_quote: the2007federal Budget allocated CAD500million for large facilities producing 'next generation' renewables

reforms.description: Canada's new Growing Forward agricultural policy framework emphasizes innovation and science as key drivers of long-term sectoral viability, replacing the Agricultural Policy Framework that expired in 2008. The framework includes a suite of new assistance programmes and focuses on enabling the agriculture and agri-food industry to seize evolving market opportunities with greater emphasis on innovation and science.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Directs public R&D and innovation support toward agricultural competitiveness and long-term sectoral sustainability, enhancing productivity and market responsiveness in a trade-exposed sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'implementation of the first part of a new framework, Growing Forward, has begun' and 'launching a new initiative in 2008 called Growing Forward'.
reforms.importance_rationale: Growing Forward represents a comprehensive, system-wide replacement of the Agricultural Policy Framework covering the entire sector. It introduces a structural shift toward innovation and science as central policy pillars, affecting federal and provincial agricultural policy across multiple commodities and regions, with significant budgetary implications.
reforms.source_quote: The next generation of agriculture and agri-food policy is being finalised, and implementation of the first part of a new framework, Growing Forward, has begun... the new framework will focus more on ensuring that the agriculture and agri-food industry can seize on evolving market opportunities in the global context, with a greater emphasis on innovation and science.

reforms.description: Canada's Agriculture Policy Framework (APF) included a science and innovation pillar designed to increase growth and profitability of the agricultural and agri-food sector through sustainable production systems, bio-products and bio-processes, and technology transfer and commercialisation of new products, including funding for sunrise industries producing bio-fuels and bio-materials.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Directs public R&D funding toward agricultural innovation, technology transfer, and commercialisation of new bio-products, which should enhance sector productivity and long-term competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: The APF was implemented in June 2003 following an agreement by agricultural ministers in 2001. The science and innovation programmes were described as operational, though many were still at an experimental stage.
reforms.importance_rationale: The APF represented a comprehensive, system-wide restructuring of Canadian agricultural policy across five pillars, with the science and innovation component explicitly designed to shift focus from short-term income support to long-term sector viability through R&D and technology commercialisation. This was a major structural reform affecting federal and provincial policy coordination.
reforms.source_quote: The science and innovation programmes, some of the most challenging in the APF, were intended to increase the potential for growth and profitability of the Canadian agriculture and agri-food sector in the long run... Under the science and innovation programming, technology transfer and the commercialisation of new products is being accelerated.

reforms.description: Canada launched an initiative to expand bio-energy production through consumption mandates (5% ethanol blend in gasoline by 2010, 2% biodiesel blend by 2012) and budgetary support of CAD 2.2 billion over nine years for operating incentives, construction of production facilities, and investment in next-generation technologies, with particular focus on second-generation cellulosic ethanol.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in cellulosic ethanol R&D supports productivity and innovation in agriculture and energy sectors, but mandates and subsidies create market distortions and may crowd out more cost-efficient renewable technologies, with uncertain net carbon benefits relative to cost.
reforms.status_evidence: In 2006 the Canadian federal government launched an initiative to mandate a 5% ethanol blend in gasoline by 2010 and a 2% biodiesel blend by 2012. Budgetary support totalling CAD 2.2 billion over nine years has been made available.
reforms.importance_rationale: Represents a major structural commitment to sectoral R&D and technology development in bio-energy, with CAD 2.2 billion investment over nine years, mandatory consumption targets, and explicit focus on next-generation cellulosic ethanol technology. Addresses multiple policy objectives (environmental, agricultural, rural development) and signals long-term strategic direction for the sector.
reforms.source_quote: in 2006 the Canadian federal government launched an initiative to mandate a 5% ethanol blend in gasoline by 2010 and a 2% biodiesel blend in on-road diesel and heating oil by 2012... Budgetary support totalling CAD 2.2 billion over nine years has been made available for operating incentives, construction of production facilities and investment in next-generation technologies.
